analysis: Examined the SSDPrefixCache.swift head text (stage, readWindowSidecars, retire/eviction/sweep/scan paths) and the SSDWholeRootMaintainer.swift patch plus base text. The only changed behavior is a new optional `unusedSince` parameter. SSDPrefixCache.retireOwnedEntries/retireIndexedEntries (~1790-1805) forwards it to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove. In SSDWholeRootMaintainer.maintain, the TTL pass calls removeOwned(expired, unusedSince: now - ttl) and passes it to SSDDiskBudget.retireActiveEntries. A loaded store can therefore keep a file whose RAM index recorded a hit after the cutoff, even though the mtime from the scan trailed it. Survivors then get their mtime re-read from the filesystem so the budget LRU ordering is not stale. Security reading (T-041, TB-007, A-001): this is a sliding-TTL correctness fix and does not extend retention beyond the 30-minute TTL. A file is kept only if the index saw a hit within the TTL window, and stage() bumps both index and mtime (lines 1578-1587). The unloaded fallback (SSDCacheEpochStore.performUnloadedDestructiveChange) has no active index, so it still expires on mtime alone. Crypto, HMAC naming, salt scoping, epoch handling and path-safety checks (removeItemIfSafe, isSafeBlockURL, no-follow I/O) are unchanged. attributesOfItem uses lstat semantics, so it does not follow symlinks for the final component. Not visible in the supplied evidence: how SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove and SSDDiskBudget.retireActiveEntries compare unusedSince against index lastAccess (strictness, and whether skipped files are correctly excluded from the returned removed set). The next pass should confirm that kept files are not reported as removed, and that an index lastAccess that can only move forward cannot hold a file past the TTL. No regression is identified from the supplied evidence.
